metadata.title: A Slogan Is a Division
metadata.topic: INFO 7375 - Chapter 1 - Randomness and first prompts
metadata.concept: A training-scale slogan restated as a division with a hidden assumption

recorded_output.mode: offline arithmetic on cited published figures

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN. The slogan lands as a question, answered by the film.
beats.narration_text: You have heard this one. It would take a person thousands of years to read everything G P T three was trained on. It sounds like a measurement. I want to show you that it is a division, and that one of its inputs is missing.

props.command: how long would it take a person to read 300 billion tokens?

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW. Writer types the misconception and corrects it.
beats.narration_text: Here is the correction up front. The reading comparison is not a measurement of the training data. It is a division. And the number it produces depends on a reading speed that the slogan never states.

props.text:
The reading comparison
is a measurement.

beats.role_note: Published figures only. Later models are larger and undisclosed.
beats.narration_text: Start with figures that were actually published. G P T three: one hundred seventy five billion parameters. About three hundred billion training tokens. And a reported training compute of three point one four times ten to the twenty third floating point operations. Those come from Brown and colleagues, twenty twenty. Later frontier models are larger, and their figures are frequently undisclosed.

meta: Reported by the authors; not re-measured here.

beats.role_note: MATH-TYPESETTING: real fraction bar, structured notation, staged reveal.
beats.narration_text: So do the arithmetic in the open. Three hundred billion tokens, at about zero point seven five words per token, is two hundred twenty five billion words. Divide that by a reading rate times the minutes in a year, and the units leave you with years. At two hundred fifty words per minute, that is one thousand seven hundred and eleven years.

props.title: The slogan, written as arithmetic
props.note: Every quantity here was published or stated. Except one.

beats.role_note: THE point of the film: the answer moves on an unstated input.
beats.narration_text: But nobody stated the reading rate. So run every rate the course script uses. At one hundred fifty words per minute, the answer is two thousand eight hundred fifty two years. At two hundred, two thousand one hundred thirty nine. At two hundred fifty, one thousand seven hundred eleven. At three hundred, one thousand four hundred twenty six. Same corpus. Same arithmetic. The answer moves by more than fourteen hundred years, and the thing that moved was an assumption nobody wrote down.

props.title: Same arithmetic. Four reading rates.
props.note: Spread: 1,425.9 years on an unstated input. Source: llm_scale.py, 2026-09-26.

beats.role_note: Second instance, so the method reads as general, not a one-off.
beats.narration_text: The compute slogan behaves the same way. If you could perform one billion operations per second by hand, G P T three's reported training compute would take you about nine point nine five million years. You may have heard over one hundred million years. That sentence needs roughly ten times G P T three's budget. Both sentences can be true. They are not the same sentence, and a reader who cannot tell them apart cannot audit either one.

lines: At one billion operations per second:
which is about 10x GPT-3 - a different model
meta: Both statements can be true. They are not the same statement.

beats.role_note: What the explanation does NOT establish. Dark = 1 of 9 beats.
beats.narration_text: Now the boundary, and it matters more than the arithmetic. None of this shows the comparison is false, or useless. Every version of it still says the same true thing: more text than a person could read in many lifetimes. What the sweep establishes is narrower than that. The headline number carries a hidden parameter, so until someone states the reading rate, you cannot check the figure you were handed. That is the entire claim. It says nothing about whether anything the model writes is true.

lines: or that the slogan should not be used.
Only that it has an input nobody stated.
meta: A hidden parameter is not a false claim.
And none of this is evidence about truthfulness of output.

beats.role_note: Your turn. The composer returns with a prompt the viewer can run.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take one impressive A I number you see this week. Parameters, tokens, energy, dollars. Restate it as a division, and name the input nobody specified. That is the whole skill.

props.command: take one AI statistic I have seen this week, rewrite it as a division, and name the input nobody stated
